A copper distillation rig dominates the central workbench — coiled tubing connects three glass alembics bubbling with amber, violet, and silver liquids. Stoppered flasks crowd the base, one still dripping luminous condensate into a catch-bowl. Tongs, a brass burner, and a cracked clay crucible fill the remaining surface.

Three enormous grimoires lie open and stacked at angles, their pages covered in dense runic script that pulses with cold blue light. Floating letters drift upward like embers above the topmost volume. Loose annotated parchments are pinned beneath inkwells, and a quill still bleeds violet ink onto an open margin.

A faceted crystal orb rests on a black iron pedestal, slowly rotating without being touched. Seven runic glyphs orbit it in a tilted ellipse, each one trailing a faint phosphorescent ribbon. Beneath the pedestal, smaller polished gemstones are arranged in a deliberate geometric pattern on a velvet-lined tray.

An iron cauldron hangs over low hearthfire, its interior churning with thick emerald potion that releases curling silver steam. Bundles of dried wolfsbane, mandrake root, and starflower hang from the hood above. Squat clay bottles and a wooden ladle are clustered on the hearthstone around the cauldron's iron feet.

A mounted wyvern skull, bleached and enormous, crowns a low oak display stand. Beneath it, a deep-crimson velvet cradle holds a single pearlescent dragon egg the size of a kettle. Three lore-tomes lie open below, their pages illustrated with anatomical scale diagrams and territorial range maps in faded sepia ink.

A shallow silver scrying-bowl sits on a fluted marble pedestal, filled with perfectly still water that glows faintly from within. Runic mist coils above the surface, spelling and unspelling fragmentary words. Two spent candle stubs and a ring of carved rune-stones encircle the pedestal's base like a consecrated border.

A long wooden rack holds forty stoppered glass vials in descending height order, each filled with luminous liquid — deep crimson, cold blue, molten gold, spectral white. Labels written in cramped wizard's script hang from each neck. A mortar, pestle, and small set of brass scales occupy the workbench beside the rack.

A brass orrery stands on a pedestal at table height, its nested rings turning in slow, independent arcs around a glowing amber bead representing the sun. Rolled and flat celestial charts are layered beneath it, corners weighted with smooth river-stones. A compass, a sighting tube, and a star-almanac bound in black leather complete the cluster.

A copper still dominates the bench — its fat-bellied base heated by a spirit lamp, its long swan-neck arching into a coiled worm submerged in a bucket of cold water. A rack of waiting empty bottles stands ready. Beside it, open recipe folios are splattered with reagent stains and held flat by a heavy iron weight.

Five grimoires of varying thickness are stacked in an unstable leaning tower, all open simultaneously, bookmarked with ribbon and bone. Glowing amber runes rise slowly from each exposed page and dissolve at eye level. An hourglass with golden sand, two worn reading lenses, and a folded star-chart are wedged between the volumes.

A teardrop-shaped obsidian crystal, nearly two feet tall, rests in a three-pronged iron cradle on the central table. Its interior clouds and clears in slow pulses, revealing shifting shapes. Four runic stones arranged in a cardinal square on the table around it vibrate faintly, connected to the crystal by thin lines of etched silver inlay.

A wide-bellied bronze cauldron squats over a ring of firelight, potion inside the color of old copper, surface creased with slow rotation. Beside it on the hearthstone: a bundle of dried serpent-tongue root, a glass jar of rendered dragon-fat, and a line of corked amber bottles already filled and sealed with wax stamps.

A dragon skull the length of a man's arm is mounted on a horizontal oak bracket, lower jaw slightly ajar to reveal rows of vestigial teeth. A speckled egg in a copper cradle sits directly before it like an offering. Beneath both, a broad folio lies open to a full-spread illustration of a dragon's skeletal musculature.

A broad silver scrying-bowl engraved with interlocking serpent borders rests on a three-legged obsidian stand. The water inside is utterly still but faintly luminous, reflecting no ceiling above it. Drifting above the surface, runic syllables form and dissolve in slow sequence. Two silver-capped ink bottles and a notation scroll flank the pedestal.

A central rack of thirty vials occupies the workbench foreground — contents ranging from viscous black to radiant citrine. Several are actively effervescent, tiny bubbles climbing the glass. Around the rack: a bone-handled dropper, a bronze funnel, a stack of ingredient logs, and three sealed stone crocks labeled in chalk on their lids.

A grand brass orrery nearly three feet wide turns at the room's center on a carved wooden pedestal. Its outermost ring carries a small moonstone bead along a tilted elliptical track. Below the pedestal, celestial charts are spread flat and overlapping, annotated in multiple ink colors and different handwriting across decades of accumulated observation.

The workbench holds a complete alchemical circuit — two alembics connected through a glass Y-junction, each receiving heat from separate spirit lamps. Liquid travels between them in a slow cycle, changing color each pass. Scattered across the remaining surface: a measuring chain, glass stirring rods, a leather journal propped open with a pewter flask.

An open lectern holds the largest tome in the room — its spine cracked from repeated use, its current double-page spread alive with glowing marginal runes that rearrange themselves slowly. Stacked on either side, four smaller volumes lie open in support. A quill stands upright in an inkwell, and a brass bookmark clip holds three loose prophecy sheets.

A crystal sphere of deep amethyst floats three inches above its iron cradle without visible support, spinning on an axis tilted at thirty degrees. Around it, orbiting runes trace overlapping circles at different speeds. On the table surface beneath, a hand-drawn diagram maps the rune positions against a list of interpretive glyphs written in silver ink.

The stone hearth supports a hammered-iron cauldron on a wrought trivet, its brew a murky teal that occasionally flashes white from beneath. Arranged on the wide hearthstone: twelve small bottles in a row, a ceramic pot of powdered nightstone, a fish-hook-shaped stirring rod, and a folded cloth for handling the cauldron's scalding rim.

A reconstructed wyvern jaw, set upright in a sand-filled stone box, frames the display's centerpiece — a mottled green egg resting inside a nest of iron filings and preserved dragonwort. To the right, two reference tomes lie open; their pages are cross-referenced with fine thread pinned between corresponding illustrations of egg development stages.

A trio of glass vial racks, each a different height, form a tiered apothecary display at the bench's center. Vials glow in graduated intensity — dimmest on the left, brightest on the right, the rightmost nearly too vivid to observe directly. A set of glass-tipped measuring pipettes, a wax-sealing kit, and a contents ledger complete the arrangement.

A hammered copper still with a distinctive double-coil condenser occupies the bench — both coils active simultaneously, producing liquids of different color into two separate receivers. A mounted diagram on a small board behind it labels every component in neat calligraphy. Open reference folios, ink-stained and dog-eared, are spread flat around the still's base.

A globe-orrery of moderate size sits on a pedestal, surrounded at its base by six parchment celestial charts weighted at corners by mineral specimens. The orrery's innermost ring carries a rose-quartz bead; its outermost a chip of dark iron meteorite. A tide-prediction almanac, bound in water-stained vellum, leans open against the pedestal's side.

Two cauldrons, one small and one large, share the same wide hearthstone over separate flame-rings. The large one steams with a rust-red reduction; the small one holds a clear simmering liquid. Between them, a wooden tray displays stoppered vials, dried herb packets tied with twine, and a brass ladle hanging from a hook driven into the fireback.
